summary: Phelps County lookout in the Mark Twain National Forest; a 1941 notice gives visitor counts, and the lookout page marks it removed with no date.

facts.status_note: The lookout history page marks the tower Removed, with no date or method given. TopoQuest lists it as historical.

events.note: Rolla Herald notice dated October 2, 1941, quoted on the Knotwell page, says a Regional Manual credited the tower as the most visited station in the 9th Region and reports visitor counts for one Sunday in October 1940 and for Easter Sunday.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific facts come from the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes a 1941 Rolla Herald notice second-hand; the original was not located. TopoQuest's coordinates (N37.872263, W91.945161) match the brief's coordinates. No build date, builder, staffing, fire or removal date was found, so none is stated. Access is omitted because no source gives it. A search summary mentioned an ExpertGPS listing of Knotwell Lookout Tower (historical) under a Liberty, MO heading; it was not read and is most likely a grouping by nearby town, not a second tower. Wikipedia gives the forest's founding date as September 11, 1939 in its text and September 23, 1939 in its infobox; the story uses the year only.
